sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Rowlatt Act (1919)**: Officially the 'Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act', it empowered the government to detain political prisoners without trial for up to two years. It was based on the **Sedition Committee Report** chaired by Justice Sidney Rowlatt.
• **Satyagraha Sabha**: Formed by Gandhi in February 1919 to organize the protest; members pledged to disobey the law and court arrest.
• **Jallianwala Bagh**: A public meeting held on Baisakhi day (April 13, 1919) to protest the arrest of Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.
• **General Dyer's Action**: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on the unarmed crowd, blocking the only exit, resulting in hundreds of deaths.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal
Prelims: Nature of the Act (Civil liberties violation)
Mains: Turning point for Gandhi's disillusionment with British justice

items.definition: The official inquiry commission set up by the British government to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; it was criticized for being a 'whitewash'.
Gandhi's method of non-violent resistance; the Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first time he utilized a nationwide strike (Hartal) as a political tool.

items.title: Major Consequences
items.content:
• **Rabindranath Tagore**: Renounced his Knighthood in protest against the massacre.
• **Gandhi's Reaction**: Returned the 'Kaiser-i-Hind' medal and realized the British government could not be trusted, leading to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of unity between Hindu-Muslim factions in some areas; violence in Punjab and Gujarat.
• **Solutions**: Gandhi called off the movement due to the violence, emphasizing the need for 'Satyagrahi' training.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'R-S-J-H' (Rowlatt, Satyagraha, Jallianwala, Hunter).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Rowlatt Act led to Satyagraha, which led to Jallianwala Bagh, which led to the Hunter Committee.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Hunter Committee' (Jallianwala Bagh) with the 'Hunter Commission' (Education, 1882). Always verify the context.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Moral Bankruptcy of the British Empire' when discussing the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

keyTakeaways: The Rowlatt Act was the first nationwide legislative protest led by Gandhi.
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was the catalyst for the end of Gandhi's cooperation with the British.
The Hunter Committee report was widely condemned by the Indian National Congress as a 'whitewash'.
